name: Maltese Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Galea, Maria. 2014. SignWriting (SW) of Maltese Sign Language (LSM) and its development into an orthography: Linguistic considerations. PhD dissertation, University of Malta. 689 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing about LSM word stress. The four 'stress' hits are about spoken languages (Coulmas 2003) or the general sign-linguistics literature (Coulter & Anderson 1993 'dynamics of movement such as stress, duration, rate'). LSM prosody is treated only at sentence level: Sec. 6.8 (pp. 236-241) and 9.7.1 (pp. 410-416) describe head-tilt patterns (UP-UP-DOWN marks a statement, UP-UP-UP marks open-ended questions/exclamations).

sources.citation: Azzopardi-Alexander, Marie. 2018. Maltese Sign Language: Parallel interwoven journeys of the Deaf community and the researchers. In Patrizia Paggio & Albert Gatt (eds.), The languages of Malta, 271-292. Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1181803
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic/historical chapter; no phonology, no mention of stress or prosody. Sec. 9 (pp. 283-287) enumerates all academic work on LSM (D'Amato 1988, Porter 1995, Azzopardi 2001, Fenech 2002, Azzopardi-Axiaq 2005, Galea 2006, Mifsud 2010, Galea 2014), none of it a phonological description.

sources.note: Only a literature-review mention of Coulter (1990) on emphatic stress in ASL (p. 7); nothing on stress in LSM.

sources.citation: Mifsud, Maria. 2010. A study of superordinates and hyponyms in Maltese Sign Language. MA thesis, University of Malta.

sources.note: Per Azzopardi-Alexander 2018 (p. 287) it analyses compounding with reduced movement, 'faster transitions of handshapes.. and durational compression' (Mifsud 2010: 150) -- the closest thing to a word-level rhythmic/prosodic description of LSM that exists.
